To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) multi-class classification can be learned with only pairwise similarity labels, (2) this is achieved by learning a binary classifier that is trained to maximize the similarity of examples from the same class, and (3) this binary classifier is a submodule of a multi-class classifier.

1) multi-class classification can be learned without multi-class labels by learning to predict pairwise similarity; 2) this can be done in the supervised, uns-supervised cross-task, or semi-supervised setting; 3) the method can be implemented using a simple neural network architecture and a novel loss function; and 4) the proposed approach achieves state of the art results in all settings, providing strong evidence that multi-class classification can indeed be learned from pairwise similarity.
